SLAP Tear (Superior Labral Tear) Treatment in Hyderabad

A SLAP tear (Superior Labrum Anterior to Posterior) is an injury to the labrum of the shoulder, the ring of cartilage that surrounds the socket. It commonly occurs in overhead athletes and can cause pain and instability. Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy specializes in shoulder arthroscopy at Apollo Hospitals, Financial District, Hyderabad.

Symptoms of SLAP Tear (Superior Labral Tear) Treatment in Hyderabad

Deep shoulder pain
Clicking or popping
Pain with overhead activities
Decreased shoulder strength
Feeling of instability

Causes of SLAP Tear (Superior Labral Tear) Treatment in Hyderabad

Overhead throwing sports (baseball, tennis)

Fall on outstretched arm

Motor vehicle accidents

Sudden pulling on the arm

Repetitive overhead activities

Age-related degeneration

Diagnosis Methods

Physical Examination

O'Brien test, biceps load test, crank test

MRI Arthrogram

Gold standard - dye injected to see labrum

Diagnostic Arthroscopy

Sometimes needed for definitive diagnosis

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I pitch again after SLAP repair?
Many athletes return to throwing after SLAP repair, though return rates to previous performance levels vary. Proper rehabilitation and mechanics correction are essential.
Do all SLAP tears need surgery?
No, many SLAP tears, especially degenerative ones in older patients, can be managed with physical therapy. Surgery is mainly for young, active patients with unstable tears.
